Changelog

v0.135, 2026-11-02

  • The starter letters and numbers are now one 5×5 pixel typeface: capitals A to Z and numbers 0 to 9, each a single piece of blocks joined edge to edge, so they all fit the default grid and Make works on every one.
  • The yellow button on step 1 names the chosen rule, for example Make you up and unmake you.
  • There are two random buttons: Random symbol (the signs and shapes) and Random character (the pixel letters and numbers).

v0.134, 2026-11-02

  • The demo page opens each round with the rule sentence choosing itself: the words spin and settle one by one (the rule, how many blocks at a time, and what follows), then the loop runs, and the next round draws a different rule.

v0.133, 2026-11-02

  • The sentence now reads "N ways I can make you up, two blocks at a time and unmake you". Two blocks at a time is where it starts, and "unmake you" is the default second word: tap it to swap it for Change or Grow, or for nothing, so the unmaking can be left out.

v0.132, 2026-11-02

  • How many blocks act at a time. After the rule, tap "one block at a time" to choose two, three or all of them. Moving two blocks gives 139 ways for the T and three or more give every other joined shape of six blocks (215); changing all six blocks at once gives 531,441 ways; growing two blocks at a time takes 3 steps and all at once takes 1. The title says the full number of ways ("1,215 ways I can change you, two blocks at a time"), while a long list on the sheet and in the book is a seeded pick of 150 from the pattern code. Unmaking stays one block at a time.

v0.131, 2026-11-02

  • Grow now builds the shape up from nothing, one block at a time, as the opposite of Unmake: "6 ways I can grow you and 6 to unmake you". The order the blocks arrive in comes from the pattern code. (It first added a block to the finished shape, which was the wrong idea.)

v0.130, 2026-11-02

  • The rule is a sentence in the control panel: "35 ways I can make you up". Tap the verb to choose Move, Change or Grow, and tap "add another rule" to follow it with a second one ("89 ways I can make you up and change you"). The second rule's ways come after the first's, and the pattern code records both.

v0.129, 2026-11-02

  • Two more rules, chosen in the control panel. Change: one block becomes another shape in the same place (a circle, or an arch or triangle in any turn), so the T has 54 ways. Grow: the shape is built up from nothing, one block at a time, so the T has 6 ways. The wording follows the rule: "54 ways I can change you", "12 ways I can grow you". The pattern code records the rule, and codes made before this are Move. Direction is hidden for Change, since it means nothing there.

v0.127, 2026-11-02

  • The book is set in Libre Franklin and Libre Baskerville Italic, drawn as outlines, so the PDF needs no fonts and looks the same in every reader. It replaces the standard PDF fonts used before.

v0.126, 2026-11-02

  • The type in the SVG downloads is drawn as outlines, in Libre Franklin and Libre Baskerville Italic, so the files look the same on any machine and need no fonts installed. This covers the contact sheet and the animated SVG.

v0.125, 2026-11-02

  • Zoom on the contact sheet preview. Open the preview and zoom with the wheel, a pinch, the + and - buttons or a double click, drag to move around, and Fit puts the whole page back.

v0.112, 2026-11-01

  • A demo page, form.pkwr.co/demo.html, for a screen or a projector. A random symbol fills the screen and runs through every iteration, making then unmaking, then another symbol is chosen. Nothing else is shown, and there are no controls.

v0.111, 2026-11-01

  • The imposed book now has 3 mm of bleed and crop marks. Each sheet is SRA4 landscape (320 by 225 mm) so the two A5 pages have room for them, with marks at the four corners and at the fold, and the trim and bleed boxes set in the PDF. The plain pages book is unchanged.

v0.105, 2026-11-01

  • Nine signs in the manner of Rudolf Koch's The Book of Signs join the random symbols: St Andrew cross, anchor, life rune, trident, sun wheel, crescent, hourglass, Lorraine cross and triple cross.

v0.103, 2026-11-01

  • Extra ways to make you up. After every single move, six more variants are added, each made by one to three moves in a row from the original. They are chosen from the pattern's code, so the same code always gives the same ones, and they are the same whichever treatment is chosen. The T now has 35 ways to make you up (29 single moves and 6 extra).

v0.102, 2026-11-01

  • Pattern code. Every pattern has a short code, for example 32753-KSWXP-J8, shown in the side panel with a Copy button. Type or paste a code under "Enter a code" to load that pattern, or open the site with ?code= and the code on the end. The same code always makes the same book, and the code is printed on the book's last page as "Pattern code". Shapes drawn in different places on the grid share a code.

v0.31, 2026-11-01

  • A video for social media, next to the GIF, in the same square (1:1) and story (9:16) shapes. It is recorded in the browser as the animation plays, repeated to run at least six seconds, and saved as MP4 where the browser can write it (Safari and current Chrome) or WebM otherwise, which Instagram and TikTok do not take. Every frame of the GIF and the video carries the title line and a small "Made with Form, form.pkwr.co" credit.

v0.30, 2026-11-01

  • Credit and terms now travel with the work. Every SVG, PDF and GIF Form makes carries "Made with Form, form.pkwr.co. © 2026 Patrick Walker", with the terms for sharing and printing, in the file itself (a description and metadata in SVGs, document properties in PDFs, a comment in GIFs), and the book's colophon states them. The About page says what people may do with what they make.

v0.28, 2026-11-01

  • A GIF for social media. It is a looping GIF of the animation, as a square (720 by 720) or a story (9:16, 720 by 1280). It is made on the device with no library, uses 32 steps between paper and ink, and takes at most 120 frames. A 93-frame square GIF is under 500 KB.

v0.23, 2026-10-31

  • Publication. Two new buttons make a book of the current shape in the design of the original publication: a cover, the five treatments each with the shape on top and its variants in a grid, dark plates with the shape and its variants, and a colophon, all A5 with no bleed. Imposed is a PDF with two pages on each A4 landscape sheet in booklet order (print double sided, flip on short edge, fold and staple). Pages is the plain A5 pages. Hidden variants are left out, and every page carries the line "N ways I can make you up" (or "unmake you").

v0.17, 2026-10-31

  • The contact sheet is a portrait page. Choose A3, A2, A1 or A0 and the variants are laid out on one page of that size, as large as they will fit, and the download is an SVG at that physical size in millimetres, ready to print. The size is in the file name. The preview on screen is the same page, so what you see is what downloads, and hidden variants are left out and the rest grow to fill the page.

v0.14, 2026-10-31

  • A start page, as on Spot: a black screen with the F mark, three blocks that keep moving and turn yellow when you point at them, the version bottom left, and a yellow Form · About strip that slides the About text out from the right. The text is read from the About page, so there is one copy.

v0.6, 2026-10-31

  • Cumulative density view: every block is drawn as fine lines, and the original and the last few variants each keep their own angle and spacing, so where they overlap the lines build into a mesh, as in the publication.

v0.2, 2026-10-31

  • Cumulative transparency view (Ghost): the variants before this one stay behind it as fading ghosts, an onion skin, so you see the path the shape has taken.

v0.1, 2026-10-31

First release.

  • Form, Direction and Cumulative Solid views, with SVG export of the animation and the contact sheet.
  • One rule from the book: one block moves per move and the place it left stays marked.
